content.text:
Confirmed. The simulator is dialing the throwaway bridge I ran for the end-to-end test, not your real one.

- The app's log shows it retrying `ws://192.168.4.54:47899/ws` and getting "Connection refused".
- Port 47899 was my temporary bridge instance, paired into the simulator via the URL I opened, and I killed it when the test finished.
- Your installed bridge is up on port 47821, but it has a different pairing token, so the simulator can't just fall over to it. Wi-Fi is fine.

Two ways forward, your call:

1. **Re-pair the simulator with the installed bridge.** Run `cmux-bridge --pair`, then I open the printed URL in the simulator with `simctl openurl` and you tap Open. This gets it connected, but the installed daemon is still the old binary, so cards will show polled text, not the live emulator.
2. **Install the new bridge first, then re-pair.** Run this from the repo (it hard-kills the old daemon and installs the build from this branch):
   ```bash
   ./scripts/install-bridge.sh --tailscale
   cmux-bridge --pair
   ```
   Then the same openurl step. This is the one that lets the simulator show live herdr frames.

Option 2 replaces your running daemon, so I haven't done it. Say which you want and I'll run it.

Connected and live. The screenshot shows the simulator rendering this very Claude Code session from herdr through the emulator: colours, the status line, the cursor, and my in-progress output at the moment the shot was taken. The app log confirms it moved from the dead port to `ws://192.168.4.54:47821/ws`, and the bridge log shows both runtimes connected plus the Tailscale listener up.

The two tiles below the focused card are the polled text path, as designed. Only the focused surface streams frames.

If you switch focus to one of the cmux surfaces you should see it drop back to the text card with no error, since cmux answers the frame subscription with `unsupported`. That's the fallback worth eyeballing next.
seems to work on this specific session but when switching surfaces to other sessions, it looks like the old way with it not being responsive
Let me check which code paths change the focused surface and whether all of them trigger the frame subscription. I'll also check what the bridge is currently observing.

content.text:
Pushed to PR #31. The cause was real: the layout picks its focused card from the pane list, which arrives after a workspace switch, but the frame stream was only re-pointed on the earlier surface-list refresh, so it stayed on the first session.

The rebuilt app is now running in the simulator with the fix. Switch between a few sessions, including a cmux one, and tell me what you see. On my side the bridge's observer should follow each herdr surface you land on, and cmux surfaces should fall back to the text card without an error.
